Clojure on the Nintendo Wii.

wii-jolt runs stock raylib 6.0, Chez Scheme and Clojure through Jolt on a Wii. Everything builds on a Mac with devkitPro in Docker, gets tested in the Dolphin emulator, and plays on the real console from the Homebrew Channel.

Get started Run it on your Wii

Four games, up to four players

How it fits together

raylib

Stock raylib 6.0 with no source changes, drawing through SDL2 and OpenGX, the OpenGL 1.x layer devkitPro ships for the Wii's GPU. raylib on the Wii

Chez Scheme

Chez's portable bytecode target, tpb32b, fits the Wii's 32-bit big-endian PowerPC. The C kernel needed a short patch and libogc's missing thread-local storage hooks. Chez Scheme on the Wii

Jolt

Jolt cross-compiles Clojure through Chez with jolt build --target tpb32b, and the fixes it needed for a 32-bit target are upstream. Jolt on the Wii

The real console

The Wii's CPU traps a misaligned double load that Dolphin lets through, so the first console run stopped every Jolt build at boot. With the kernel fix, Balloon Pop and Super Mona play with a real Wiimote.

The guide reads best in order, from the toolchain through each layer to the games. The project went open source live at clj-aus #2, and the slides from that talk tell the story.
